name: @appstrate/mcpemails
description: Mailbox integration backed by the hosted MCP Emails server (mcpemails.com/api/mcp) — one MCP surface over Gmail, Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Yandex and any IMAP/SMTP account the user connects on mcpemails.com. The sidecar opens a Streamable HTTP MCP client (protocol 2025-06-18) and injects the actor's OAuth2 access token as `Authorization: Bearer …`. Authorization is fully standards-based, so no OAuth app is registered by hand: RFC 9728 protected-resource discovery on /api/mcp, RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata on the mcpemails.com issuer, RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration as a public client (`token_endpoint_auth_method: none`) and RFC 7636 PKCE (S256); the operator installs the connector and each member clicks Connect. Niveau-2 scope model applies: the nine upstream scopes are catalogued and per-tool `required_scopes` drive incremental consent, so an agent only asks for what its selected tools need. The authorization server issues a refresh token on every authorization-code exchange with no offline scope or authorize parameter to ask for one (`refresh_token_issuance: "default"`); access tokens live an hour, refresh tokens are one-time-use and rotate on each exchange under a sliding 180-day window, so the platform's token-refresh service must persist each rotated refresh token. Phase 4 (per-tool URL envelope) is N/A — every tool transits the same /api/mcp endpoint, and the upstream's per-key inbox allowlist plus workspace roles are the only gates. Mail is fetched live per call and never stored upstream; there are no webhooks or server-initiated events, so an agent that must react to new mail polls `email_read` with `action: "list"` on a schedule. Rate limits are per key (100 req/min, 1 000/h, 10 000/day) under a plan ceiling (Free 60/min through Team 1 000/min), and the Free plan meters 150 email actions a month.

scope_catalog.label: Identity
scope_catalog.description: Upstream treats openid and email as identity scopes, kept apart from the tool scopes: they gate nothing, and without one of them /api/oauth/userinfo returns the opaque user id alone. Both are in default_scopes because the connection label IS the account id, so dropping them costs a readable name.

scope_catalog.label: Email address
scope_catalog.description: Lets /api/oauth/userinfo return the account's email (and email_verified), which is what names the connection in the UI.

scope_catalog.label: Read mail
scope_catalog.description: List inboxes and folders; list, read and search messages; read signatures.

scope_catalog.label: Search mail (narrow)
scope_catalog.description: Vestigial upstream: no tool requires it on its own, read:email already gates email_read's search action. Kept in the catalog because keys and consents issued earlier carry it.

scope_catalog.label: Send mail
scope_catalog.description: Send, reply and forward; set signatures; review and decide held sends.

scope_catalog.label: Organize mail
scope_catalog.description: Create, rename and delete folders/labels; move, copy, flag and archive messages, including search-and-move sweeps.

scope_catalog.label: Delete mail
scope_catalog.description: Move messages to Trash or hard-delete them, including search-and-delete sweeps. Irreversible when permanent.

scope_catalog.label: Manage drafts
scope_catalog.description: Create, read, update and delete unsent messages, and drive the draft-editor card.

scope_catalog.label: Search contacts
scope_catalog.description: Find people by name or email address.

scope_catalog.label: Schedule sends
scope_catalog.description: Queue messages for future delivery and manage the queue.

scope_catalog.label: Manage automations
scope_catalog.description: Read and write standing, unattended inbox rules. Strictly more power than any interactive write scope — upstream refuses it to workspace viewers.
